docs.body:
### Workshops
[Muddy Anvil](#muddy-anvil) (Blacksmith) - Build and upgrade your forge to craft superior tools, unlock advanced smelting recipes, and expand your metalworking capabilities!

[Bubbling Barrel](#bubbling-barrel) (Alchemist) - Build and upgrade your laboratory to brew powerful potions, master glass blowing techniques, and discover rare alchemical materials!

[Gleaming Nest](#gleaming-nest) (Jeweler) - Build and upgrade your workshop to craft exquisite jewelry, improve success rates, and unlock precious gem-working techniques!

[Mystic Mirror](#mystic-mirror) (Oracle) - Build and upgrade your sanctum to identify mysterious items, unlock ancient recipes, and expand your mystical knowledge.

[Critter Quest Guides](/critters-quest-docs/critter-quest-guides.md#town-building-system)

### World Map
The World Map represents the vast open world of Valdara where players venture beyond their towns to explore, gather resources, and engage with the broader game world. This expansive landscape serves as the primary arena for resource collection, PVP encounters, and territorial control, connecting all players within a shared persistent environment. Resource nodes spawn throughout the map providing different materials that Critters can gather, while other players' towns dot the landscape, each representing unique settlements and potential allies or rivals in your journey through Valdara.

The world contains diverse challenges and opportunities including formidable world bosses that require strategic planning and powerful Critters to defeat, roaming monsters that provide PVE combat encounters and valuable loot, and the prestigious World Bank—a major territorial objective that serves as a focal point for large-scale PVP competition. Different regions across Valdara offer unique characteristics, resource types, and environmental challenges, with access to new areas unlocking as your town level progresses and your influence expands.

Navigation through the World Map requires strategic thinking as players must balance resource gathering efficiency, combat readiness, and territorial positioning. The interconnected nature of the world means that actions taken in one region can influence opportunities and conflicts in others, creating a dynamic ecosystem where economic, social, and military considerations all play crucial roles in long-term success. This integrated approach makes the World Map feel like a living, breathing world where every expedition contributes to your overall progression and standing within the broader Valdara community.

### Withdraw
**Withdraw:** Transfer assets from your Town Bank back to your connected wallet once your bank is built and withdrawal limits allow.

### Health Potions
Brewed at the Bubbling Barrel (Alchemist), health potions restore a flat amount of HP to a Critter in combat: Minor +75 (L1), Mid +150 (L3), Major +300 (L6), Mythical +800 (L9). Each recipe also requires a glass vial (Basic, Enhanced, or Crystal).

### Newcomer Shield
A free 72-hour raid shield applied automatically the first time you place your town. It is granted once, on first placement only. Moving or re-placing a town later does not grant a new one.

### Quick Shield
An instant, on-demand raid shield: 100 $QUEST for 4 hours, with 2 rolling charges (each frees up 24h after use). Protection can extend up to 24h ahead. Paid from your Town Bank or connected wallet. It cannot be raised during War Fever.

### Titan's Shield
A potion brewed at the Bubbling Barrel. A single dose grants your entire town 24 hours of raid immunity. It unlocks at Alchemist L5, costs 250 $QUEST and 12h to craft, and requires a Steel Ingot plus an Enhanced Glass Vial. Single dose, non-stacking, and blocked during War Fever.

docs.title: Town Durability & Repair
docs.heading: Town Durability & Repair
docs.body:
### Town Durability & Repair
Town and walls share a maximum durability pool that grows as you upgrade them. Raids and wear reduce it, and a town stays fully operational at or above 15%. Repair costs 0.025 $QUEST plus materials per point, with more material types required as your level rises. Full Repair fixes everything; Partial Repair fixes a chosen number of points.

### War Fever
Attacking another town puts your own into a War Fever state during which you cannot raise any shield. This stops raiders from attacking and then hiding. Each attack adds 10 minutes (capped at 30), and attacking also immediately drops your own active shield.

docs.title: What is a Master Edition NFT?
docs.heading: What is a Master Edition NFT?
tags: what is a master edition nft
docs.body:
What is a Master Edition NFT?
 A Master Edition NFT is a special, limited-edition NFT that grants its owner control over the creation and minting of up to 15 Clone NFTs. In the Critters universe, Master Edition holders enjoy exclusive rights such as setting mint prices, earning royalties from Clone sales and trades, and accessing locked $QUEST tokens.

docs.title: How many Master Edition NFTs are there?
docs.heading: How many Master Edition NFTs are there?
tags: how many master edition nfts are there
docs.body:
How many Master Edition NFTs are there?
 There are 3,500 Master Edition NFTs total. Master Edition minting has ended forever. The community voted to burn 2.1 billion leftover tokens from the mint, ensuring no additional Master Editions will ever be created. Each Master Edition allows the holder to mint up to 15 Clone NFTs, making the potential total number of NFTs 56,000 (including both Master Editions and Clones).

docs.title: What's the difference between OG and Standard Master Editions?
docs.heading: What's the difference between OG and Standard Master Editions?
docs.body:
What's the difference between OG and Standard Master Editions?
 OG Master Editions (#1-2500): Have access to free multiplier spins if not already claimed during the original mint
 Standard Master Editions (#2501-3500): Do not have multiplier access, but are eligible for a potential 2.5 SOL refund if certain conditions are met in the future

docs.title: How do I control Clone minting?
docs.heading: How do I control Clone minting?
tags: how do i control clone minting
docs.body:
How do I control Clone minting?
 As a Master Edition owner, you don't mint Clone NFTs yourself. Instead, you control the public minting process by deciding how many Clone NFTs to release from your Master Edition, within the limit of 15 per Master Edition. This minting process is handled on a dedicated Clone Mint Page, where other users can mint from your Master Edition.

docs.title: Can Clones be lost or burned?
docs.heading: Can Clones be lost or burned?
tags: can clones be lost or burned
docs.body:
Can Clones be lost or burned?
 Yes, Clone NFTs can be lost or burned during gameplay, which permanently reduces the total supply. If a Clone NFT is burned, its specific edition number is permanently lost. However, you can reopen the mint for that slot, allowing a new Clone to be minted—assuming your Master Edition has more mints available.

docs.title: What royalties do I earn?
docs.heading: What royalties do I earn?
docs.body:
What royalties do I earn?
 As a Master Edition owner, you automatically receive royalties from Clone NFTs minted from your Master Edition. Additionally, you earn royalties from secondary market sales of Clone NFTs. The base royalty is 50%, which can be boosted up to 75% with multipliers. Each Master Edition has a connected wallet that receives these payments directly.

docs.title: What happens to burned Clone NFTs?
docs.heading: What happens to burned Clone NFTs?
tags: what happens to burned clone nfts
docs.body:
What happens to burned Clone NFTs?
 Once a Clone NFT is burned, the edition number is permanently lost, and a new NFT minted from the same Master Edition will not carry the same number. This makes low-number Clones highly collectible and adds value to early mints. While the overall supply may shrink due to burning, Master Edition holders have the power to reopen their mints to issue new NFTs, as long as their Master Edition still has remaining mints.

docs.title: Can Master Edition NFTs be burned?
docs.heading: Can Master Edition NFTs be burned?
tags: can master edition nfts be burned
docs.body:
Can Master Edition NFTs be burned?
 No, Master Edition NFTs cannot be burned or lost. They remain a permanent part of the Critters universe, ensuring that Master Edition holders always have control over Edition mints and remain key players in the NFT ecosystem.

docs.title: Can I rename my Master Edition NFT?
docs.heading: Can I rename my Master Edition NFT?
tags: can i rename my master edition nft
docs.body:
Can I rename my Master Edition NFT?
 Yes, you can rename your Master Edition NFT using $QUEST tokens. This renaming feature also changes the names of all the Clone NFTs derived from it. Future owners of the Master Edition can rename it as well.

docs.title: Can I sell my Master Edition NFT?
docs.heading: Can I sell my Master Edition NFT?
tags: can i sell my master edition nft
docs.body:
Can I sell my Master Edition NFT?
 Yes, you can sell your Master Edition NFT on secondary markets. When sold, the buyer gains all the rights associated with that Master Edition, including the ability to mint any remaining Clone NFTs, claim royalties from future sales, and access to the locked $QUEST tokens.

docs.title: What happens if I don’t use all my 15 Clone mints?
docs.heading: What happens if I don’t use all my 15 Clone mints?
docs.body:
What happens if I don’t use all my 15 Clone mints?
 If you don't use all of your 15 Clone mints, the remaining mints are tied to your Master Edition. If you decide to sell your Master Edition before using all the mints, the new owner will inherit the remaining mints and can mint the rest of the Clone NFTs.

docs.title: Town stars - what they appear to be (UNCONFIRMED)
docs.heading: Town stars - what they appear to be (UNCONFIRMED)
docs.body:
**Status: community observation, not documented.** The official docs never connect the word "stars" to towns - every star reference in the documentation is about the Critter promotion system (0.2 increments up to 5.0, earned by consuming clones).

Players report a star meter on their **town** that fills as critters gather and return, reaching 5/5.

The leading theory is that this displays **town maturity**, also called loot-ripeness, which IS documented on the Raiding & PvP page. Maturity scales how much a successful raider steals from your Town Bank - a wipe win takes up to 30%, an HP win up to 15%, and maturity determines where in that range you land. The docs state a freshly raided town has little ripe loot and regenerates ripeness over about a day.

**If this theory is right, 5/5 stars is a warning rather than an achievement** - it means your town is at maximum lootability. The counterplay would be shielding, withdrawing to your wallet, or spending the bank down before going offline.

**How to confirm:** watch whether the stars drop after you are raided or after you spend your Town Bank down. If they track your bank balance and reset after a hit, it is maturity. If they do not move, it is something else. Please report findings in Discord.

docs.title: Gacha spins are earned, not a daily free allowance
docs.heading: Gacha spins are earned, not a daily free allowance
docs.body:
A common misreading. The Gacha Wheels page says the Blue Wheel is **free**, which means **spinning costs no $QUEST** - it does NOT mean you receive free spins on a daily timer.

Per the Events System page, spins are **earned through participation in Beta tasks, quests, or staking progress**. You can spin one at a time or in bulk up to 25, and a counter shows how many you have remaining. Both wheels live in the **Events area**.

There is no documented daily free spin. Plan voucher income around how many spins you can actually earn, not around a daily faucet.
